target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures state that property and equipment are stated at cost (less accumulated depreciation in 2024) and depreciated using the straight-line method based on estimated useful lives (3-5 years in 2023, 3-7 years in 2024). D040 cites P045_S001 and P045_S002; D050 cites P052_S001 and P052_S002.

Both disclosures cover the derecognition of assets upon retirement/disposition (removing cost and accumulated depreciation, recording gain/loss) and the amortization of finance lease assets and leasehold improvements. D040 cites P045_S003, P045_S005, and P045_S006; D051 cites P052_S003, P052_S005, and P052_S006.

comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting Policy for Property and Equipment
comparisons.peer_summary: Property and equipment are stated at cost, with depreciation and amortization calculated on a straight-line basis over estimated useful lives of 2 to 15 years for equipment, 34 to 44 years for buildings, and based on the shorter of lease terms or useful lives for leasehold improvements.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies state property and equipment at cost and use the straight-line depreciation method. However, they differ significantly in their estimated useful lives for buildings. NVDA estimates building lives 'up to thirty years', whereas AMD uses a longer range of '34 to 44 years' for buildings. For equipment, NVDA uses 'three to seven years' while AMD uses a broader range of 'two to 15 years'.
